en.title: How to Read an Appointment Letter and Employment Contract
en.directAnswer: Read an employment document before signing. Check the job title, salary, probation, working hours, leave, benefits, notice, termination terms, confidentiality and workplace policies. A contract cannot always remove rights that a mandatory labour law gives to a covered worker.

atAGlance.whoFor: A worker wants a plain-language contract checklist.
atAGlance.legalBasis: Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 as amended; Bangladesh Labour (Amendment) Act, 2026; EPZ Labour Act, 2019 where applicable.
atAGlance.mainRule: Not every person called an “employee” is covered by every provision of the Labour Act. Coverage and worker status must be checked.
atAGlance.updateStatus: LAW UPDATED: cite the 2026 Labour Amendment Act, not the repealed 2025 amendment ordinance, as the current amendment layer.

en.lawMeaning: Not every person called an “employee” is covered by every provision of the Labour Act. Coverage and worker status must be checked. This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Check job title and work location.
evidence: Offer letter; appointment letter; policy handbook; salary schedule; ID; later HR changes.
en.simpleExample: A company verbally promises a bonus but the appointment letter says nothing about it. The worker should ask for important promised terms in writing before relying on them.
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: not keeping a copy.
Common mistakes: assuming “company policy” can override every statutory right.
Common mistakes: sharing confidential documents publicly..
